task: multi-object tracking from frame detections to complete trajectories under crowded occlusion
inputs: detections per frame with bbox coordinates and confidence
ground truth in simulated_sequence.json for evaluation
outputs: identity labels and bounding box sequences across frames
comparison of SparseTrack-inspired hierarchical association versus ByteTrack-like baseline
scientific_targets: decompose dense target sets into sparse subsets via pseudo-depth estimation

related_work_refresh.SORT: online tracking-by-detection commonly uses Kalman/constant-velocity prediction, IoU costs, and Hungarian assignment; related_work/paper_000.pdf
related_work_refresh.ByteTrack: central baseline: associate high-score detections first and recover occluded objects by matching low-score boxes to tracklets; related_work/paper_001.pdf
related_work_refresh.BoT-SORT: reinforces association metrics MOTA/IDF1/HOTA and SORT-like limitations; related_work/paper_002.pdf
related_work_refresh.YOLOX: detector context only; detections are supplied by dataset, not trained here; related_work/paper_003.pdf

actual_data_note: simulated_sequence.json contains 100 frames and 200 ground-truth objects per frame, not the 40/20 numbers stated in the brief; analysis uses the file contents.
